title: Krishna Sends Wedding Gifts to the Pandavas
one_line_summary: After the Pandavas marry Draupadi, Krishna sends lavish wedding presents of gold, gems, robes, servants, elephants, horses and coins, which Yudhishthira joyfully accepts.
source_excerpt: After the sons of Pandu had been married, Hari (Krishna) sent unto them (as presents) various gold ornaments set with pearls and black gems (lapis lazuli). And Madhava (Krishna) also sent unto them costly robes manufactured in various countries... The slayer of Madhu, of immeasurable soul, also sent them coins of pure gold by crores upon crores in separate heaps. And Yudhishthira the just, desirous of gratifying Govinda, accepted all those presents with great joy.

title: Krishna Counsels the Pandavas to Return to Their Kingdom
one_line_summary: At Vidura's visit, Krishna (Vasudeva) advises that the Pandavas should accept their ancestral kingdom, and Drupada defers to his judgment.
source_excerpt: Then Vasudeva said, 'I am of opinion that the Pandavas should go. But we should all abide by the opinion of king Drupada who is conversant with every rule of morality.' ... Kunti's son Yudhishthira himself doth not seek the welfare of the Pandavas so earnestly as, Kesava, that tiger among men.

title: Krishna Settles the Pandavas in Indraprastha and Returns to Dwaravati
one_line_summary: After the Pandavas receive half the kingdom, Krishna helps them establish Indraprastha, then takes his leave and returns to Dwaravati with Balarama.
source_excerpt: And, O monarch, having settled the Pandavas there, the heroic Krishna, obtaining their leave, came back with Rama to Dwaravati.

title: Krishna Appears in Answer to Draupadi's Prayer
one_line_summary: When Durvasa arrives with ten thousand disciples and Draupadi has no food to offer, she prays to Krishna, who instantly leaves Rukmini's bed and comes to her.
source_excerpt: The great and sovereign God, and Lord of the earth, of mysterious movements, the lord Kesava who is ever kind to the dependents, adored by Krishna, and perceiving her difficulty, instantly repaired to that place leaving the bed of Rukmini who was sleeping by his side.

title: Krishna Eats a Single Grain and Satisfies Durvasa and His Disciples
one_line_summary: Krishna finds one grain of rice sticking to Draupadi's vessel, eats it, and by that act the sage Durvasa and his ten thousand disciples feel their stomachs full and flee.
source_excerpt: he looked into it and saw a particle of rice and vegetable sticking at its rim. And swallowing it he said unto her, 'May it please the god Hari, the soul of the Universe, and may that god who partaketh at sacrifices, be satiated with this.' ... these ascetics, having plunged into the river, were rubbing their bodies and observing that they all felt their stomachs to be full.

title: Krishna Reassures the Pandavas and Departs
one_line_summary: After the frightened Munis flee, Krishna appears to the anxious Pandavas, assures them that Durvasa is gone and that the virtuous never suffer, then returns home.
source_excerpt: the illustrious Krishna suddenly appeared to them and addressed them these words: 'Knowing, ye sons of Pritha, your danger from that wrathful Rishi, I was implored by Draupadi to come, and (therefore) have I come here speedily. But now ye have not the least fear from the Rishi Durvasa... Virtuous men never suffer. I now ask your permission to let me return home.'

title: The Pandavas Charge Krishna with the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Before his departure for Hastinapura, Bhima, Arjuna and Nakula each address Krishna, urging him to seek peace with the Kauravas and entrusting their cause to him.
source_excerpt: O Krishna, strive thou, therefore, to bring about peace with the foe. Thou, O hero, art the foremost of all friends of both the Pandavas and the Kurus... As soon as thou goest thither, it will be accomplished.
notes: The Pandavas' parting counsel spans sections 76 (Bhima), 78 (Arjuna) and 80 (Nakula); Krishna is the central addressee being dispatched on the peace mission, but does not himself speak in these sections. Cited to section 78.

title: Karna Worships Krishna and Takes His Leave
one_line_summary: On the road from Hastinapura, Karna worships Krishna and recounts omens and visions foretelling the Kauravas' defeat; Krishna replies that the destruction of the earth is at hand, and the two part.
source_excerpt: Hearing these beneficial and auspicious words of Kesava, Karna worshipped Krishna, the slayer of Madhu... 'Indeed, the destruction of the earth is at hand when my words, O Karna, do not become acceptable to thy heart...' Having spoken these words, Karna closely pressed Madhava to his bosom. Dismissed by Kesava, he then descended from the car.
notes: Task description says Karna 'receives a boon' here, but this section contains no boon — only Karna's worship, his omen-discourse, Krishna's reply, and their parting. The boon episode is not in this section.

title: Krishna Returns to Upaplavya and Reports the Failure of the Peace Mission
one_line_summary: Krishna returns from Hastinapura and reports to the Pandavas that Duryodhana rejected his true and beneficial words in the assembly.
source_excerpt: Coming back to Upaplavya from Hastinapura, that chastiser of foes, Kesava, represented unto the Pandavas all that had happened... Vasudeva said, 'Having gone to Nagapura, I addressed Dhritarashtra's son in the assembly such words as were true, reasonable, and beneficial. That wicked minded fellow did not, however, accept them.'

title: Krishna Names Dhrishtadyumna Commander of the Pandava Army
one_line_summary: When Yudhishthira asks who should lead the seven Akshauhinis, Krishna approves the candidates and names Dhrishtadyumna as the commander-in-chief.
source_excerpt: the lotus-eyed Krishna said, eyeing Dhananjaya, the while, 'O king, I fully approve of all those powerful warriors whom ye have named for becoming the leaders of thy troops... As regards our leader, I would name that chastiser of foes, Dhrishtadyumna.'

title: Krishna Declares That War Is Now Inevitable
one_line_summary: Pressed by Yudhishthira for guidance, Krishna answers that Duryodhana bears no good will and that, since the Pandavas will not abandon their property, war must now take place.
source_excerpt: Krishna replied, in a voice deep as that of the clouds or cymbals, saying, '...That wicked-souled wight beareth no good will towards thee... As regards ourselves, we do not desire to make peace with the Kauravas by abandoning our property. War, therefore, is that which should now take place.'

title: Krishna Is Chosen as Arjuna's Charioteer
one_line_summary: As the Pandavas marshal their army for Kurukshetra, Krishna is chosen as Arjuna's guide and the driver of his steeds.
source_excerpt: And handsome Janardana endued with great intelligence, he who was the younger brother of Sankarshana, was chosen as the guide of Arjuna and the driver of his steeds.

title: Balarama Refuses to Take Sides and Departs on Pilgrimage
one_line_summary: Balarama, unwilling to fight against either the Pandavas or Duryodhana, declares he follows Krishna's cause but departs to the Saraswati tirthas rather than watch the Kauravas' destruction.
source_excerpt: As regards myself, I dare not cast my eyes on the world without Krishna (on my side). It is for this that I follow whatever Krishna seeketh to achieve... I shall now repair to the tirtha of the Saraswati for ablutions, for I shall not be able to behold with indifference the destruction of the Kauravas.
notes: The actor is Balarama, but Krishna is the central pivot of his decision (his refusal to oppose Krishna). Included as a Krishna-story beat.

title: Krishna Consoles Yudhishthira After the First Day's Battle
one_line_summary: Distraught at Bhishma's slaughter of his army, Yudhishthira speaks of retiring to the woods; Krishna consoles him and points to Sikhandin as Bhishma's destined slayer.
source_excerpt: Beholding the son of Pandu stricken with grief and deprived of his senses by sorrow, Govinda then gladdening all the Pandavas said, 'Do not grieve, O chief of the Bharatas... This Sikhandin, O thou of mighty arms, who is certainly the slayer of Bhishma.'

title: Krishna Drives Arjuna's Chariot Against Bhishma
one_line_summary: At Arjuna's bidding, Krishna drives the chariot straight toward Bhishma; in the ensuing duel Bhishma strikes Krishna himself between the breasts with three arrows.
source_excerpt: Unto him Vasudeva then said, 'Be careful, O Dhananjaya, for I will soon take thee, O hero, towards the grandsire's car.' Having said this, O king, Saurin took that car... before the car of Bhishma... Then, O king, Bhishma, that foremost of smiters, struck Vasudeva between his two breasts with three arrows.

title: Krishna Seizes His Discus and Charges Bhishma
one_line_summary: Unable to bear Bhishma's slaughter of the Pandava army, Krishna abandons the chariot reins, leaps down with the discus Sudarshana, and rushes impetuously toward Bhishma to slay him.
source_excerpt: Vasudeva's son, abandoning (the reins of) the steeds, jumped down from the car, whirling with his (right) arm his discus of beautiful nave with edge sharp as a razor, effulgent as the sun... the high-souled Krishna rushed impetuously towards Bhishma... like a lion from desire of slaying upon a prince of elephants blinded with fury.

title: Arjuna Restrains Krishna, Who Relents and Returns to the Chariot
one_line_summary: Arjuna seizes the enraged Krishna and stops him at the tenth step, vowing not to withdraw from the fight; Krishna is gratified, returns to the chariot, and sounds the Panchajanya.
source_excerpt: jumping down from his car, Partha, himself of massive and long arms, quickly ran on foot after that chief of Yadu's race... and seized him by his two hands... succeeded, O king, in stopping him with difficulty at the tenth step... 'Quell this wrath of thine. Thou art the refuge of the Pandavas, O Kesava. I swear... I will not withdraw from the acts to which I have pledged myself.' Hearing that promise and oath of his, Janardana became gratified.
